I will keep all 1.1 mu in stevia this year. My land is small, I already know this crop, and with some family members working off-farm I do not want to spread labor across different crops. At the start of the season, I will use improved seedling material because I want steadier growth and better leaf yield than old local stock, but I will still keep management simple and practical. I will prepare the field with rotary tillage since that is faster and fits my small plot well. For fertilizer, I will not push too hard because too much nitrogen can make the plants grow overly lush and hurt leaf quality, so I will use moderate nitrogen and support it with phosphorus and potassium for root growth and leaf formation. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate several times through the season to help establishment and summer growth, but I will not overwater. I will spray pesticides only when needed, and I expect a moderate yield that matches my land size, experience, and labor conditions.
